transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-01-11 15:00 PST | Duration 42m | Attendees: Alex Kim, Priya Desai (Redwood); Marco Ruiz, Leah Chen, Samir Patel (Vento)

00:00:00 - Alex Kim: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll do a quick intros then, uh, high level partnership goals.
00:00:12 - Marco Ruiz: yeah thanks Alex, excited to chat, I'm Marco, I run partnerships at Vento, we do GPU hosting focused on low-latency inference and hybrid private racks.
00:00:28 - Leah Chen: Leah here, solutions architect, I'll be the technical point for integrations.
00:00:34 - Alex Kim: awesome, Priya is our systems SE, she'll cover runtime and benchmarking. Priya?
00:00:41 - Priya Desai: hi all, hi, nice to meet you, uh quick agenda: partner fit, tech overlaps, security/compliance, potential pilot path.
00:00:55 - Samir Patel: quick note - curious how Redwood handles private deployments and on-prem models, that's core for a few customers.
00:01:07 - Priya Desai: yep, we have Redwood Private which can run in a customer VPC or on-prem with a private control plane, supports KMS integration, SSO, and audit logs.
00:01:22 - Marco Ruiz: ok cool, and for your hosted offering, what kind of tenancy and billing models do you have, like reserved pools?
00:01:33 - Alex Kim: hosted API is per-token, embeddings etc, but for partners we often talk Redwood Dedicated - reserved GPU pools, monthly commits, and partner pricing for co-sells.
00:01:47 - Marco Ruiz: got it.
00:01:50 - 00:02:05 Speaker 1 (Samir?): can you tell us about typical perf numbers, e.g., 8k seq throughput on A100-ish hardware, and how caching/batching impacts latency?
00:02:06 - Priya Desai: sure, um so runtime picks optimized kernels and has continuous batching and prefix KV cache; in our benchmarks we see 2-3x throughput for bursty chat workloads due to efficient batching, latency depends on model variant and batch policy.
00:02:29 - Leah Chen: you mentioned KV cache - how is that preserved for multi-tenant setups, and is it encrypted at rest?
00:02:39 - Priya Desai: KV cache is per-request session and can be stored in encrypted storage; for private customers they manage KMS/HSM keys, for hosted we integrate with our KMS and it's encrypted at rest. sometimes transcriber reads KMS as KMSH, ha.
00:02:59 - Marco Ruiz: ha, fair. On the hardware side we run a mix of Vento-optimized GPU nodes, mostly Ampere/late-gen, NVIDA A100 and H100 - we heard Redwood has quantization recommendations; how tightly coupled are those to specific kernels?
00:03:20 - Priya Desai: quant profiles are workload-specific; we recommend quantization levels and provide an Optimize profile that suggests int8 or bfloat16 where safe. Kernel selection is automatic but for private you can pin kernels or force a path if needed.
00:03:37 - Samir Patel: what's the fallback behavior if a model variant isn't available in a region during peak?
00:03:43 - Alex Kim: smart routing - policy-based routing by latency/cost/region; automatic fallback to compatible variants or cross-region fallback if allowed by the customer's policy.
00:03:56 - 00:04:15 Marco Ruiz: interesting - partner ask: we'd like to provide a combined offering where Vento supplies the infra and Redwood sits as the inference runtime for customers who want both managed and private. Do you have partner APIs for provisioning or telemetry?
00:04:16 - Priya Desai: we expose admin APIs for model deployment, per-route config, and telemetry hooks; console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns and tracing. We can also ship a partner SDK for provisioning.
00:04:36 - Leah Chen: for compliance, do you have SOC 2 and ISO attestation? and how about audit log retention windows?
00:04:45 - Alex Kim: yes SOC2 Type 2, ISO in progress for some regions, and audit log retention can be configured - enterprise customers can bump retention or stream logs to their SIEM. we'll send you the security pack.
00:05:00 - Marco Ruiz: perfect, please send.
00:05:05 - 00:05:35 Samir Patel: can we discuss pricing mechanics - for a partner-resold bundle is it a revenue share or resale with committed capacity? Also curious on blind spots: e.g., GPU-level telemetry access for Vento ops.
00:05:36 - Alex Kim: we do both models; typically Dedicated is a commit contract with partner discounts and revenue share on resale. For telemetry we can share aggregated infra metrics and integrate with partner monitoring endpoints, but raw host-level access is limited for security.
00:05:59 - Leah Chen: that makes sense.
00:06:05 - Priya Desai: on benchmarks, if you share a sample workload we can run Redwood performance tests on a representative Vento node. we usually run latency p95, token/s throughput, and cost-per-1k tokens.
00:06:18 - Marco Ruiz: ok we'll send a sample config, thanks.
00:06:24 - 00:06:45 Speaker 2 (Marco): small question on data residency: we have clients in EU that require data never leaves region. Does Redwood support region-locking?
00:06:46 - Alex Kim: yes, region pinning and data residency controls are supported; for Hosted we have region-specific endpoints, for Private it's entirely customer-controlled.
00:06:58 - Samir Patel: any customer references for a similar partner program?
00:07:02 - Alex Kim: we recently partnered with Aurora GPU Systems and Stratus - we'll share case study links.
00:07:08 - 00:07:30 Priya Desai: technical deep-dive items we should cover in follow-up: kernel/compilation behavior, quantization safety tests, autoscaling and burst capacity, and how we handle KV cache eviction under mem pressure.
00:07:40 - Leah Chen: can you run a quick high-level on how autoscaling works for Dedicated - policies vs burst?
00:07:47 - Priya Desai: dedicated pools have configurable autoscaling policies and optional burst capacity; autoscaler looks at queue length, latency SLO breaches, and scales nodes up, there's also a warm pool for fast spin-up.
00:08:04 - Marco Ruiz: what's the typical spin-up time for a warm node?
00:08:08 - Priya Desai: warm pools are seconds-level; cold starts can be a few minutes depending on image and model warmup.
00:08:16 - 00:08:45 Speaker 3 (Leah): on the model side, do you support both open and private model catalogs, and can partners bring their own model artifacts?
00:08:46 - Alex Kim: yes, model catalog supports open-source models and private model registries; partners can bring their own models and we support pinned versions and rollout policies.
00:08:59 - Samir Patel: any constraints on model formats? torchscript, ONNX, etc?
00:09:03 - Priya Desai: we support PyTorch HF-style models, optimized traces, and ONNX where applicable; we'll share the model onboarding doc.
00:09:12 - 00:09:40 Marco Ruiz: liability/legal question: if we're reselling and hosting customers using Redwood runtime, who holds the SLA to the end customer?
00:09:42 - Alex Kim: typically the contractual model is flexible - reseller can hold SLA and Redwood provides a platform SLA upstream, or Redwood can be the SLA holder in co-managed deals. legal will need to discuss details.
00:09:58 - Leah Chen: understood.
00:10:05 - 00:10:45 Priya Desai: quick note on performance: we'll need a representative prompt set and sequences; chat-style workloads benefit most from KV cache and batching, while long-seq generation benefits from optimized kernels and quantization. sometimes transcripts read 'KV cache' as 'KV cash' in notes, ha.
00:10:58 - Marco Ruiz: haha.
00:11:10 - 00:11:40 Samir Patel: what's the minimal integration effort for an initial pilot - e.g., can we run Redwood's runtime as a container on our nodes with minimal changes?
00:11:41 - Priya Desai: yes, Private distro can be run as containerized runtime that connects to the control plane; we also offer an air-gapped package. initial pilot usually takes 2-4 weeks for a basic workload.
00:12:00 - Alex Kim: we should set expectations: security review, network config (VPC peering or private link), and access to a test cluster.
00:12:11 - 00:12:40 Marco Ruiz: ok we'll coordinate our network team. We'll also want co-branding guidelines for a joint offering.
00:12:45 - Alex Kim: marketing and partner team will send a co-branding kit.
00:12:52 - 00:13:30 Priya Desai: technical notes for follow-up: we'll want to run a stress test with concurrency patterns, list of models you plan to host, and any custom kernel requirements. We'll include a benchmark sheet link (sent after meeting).
00:13:40 - Samir Patel: can you share the patch for RBAC integration and partner roles? We have multi-tenant customers and need role separation.
00:13:50 - Alex Kim: yes, Redwood supports RBAC and fine-grained roles; we'll attach docs.
00:14:00 - 00:15:00 Marco Ruiz: (talking about go-to-market) target customers where this co-offer fits: fintech needing low latency, healthcare needing private deployments, and gaming. also ask about sales motion - do you expect Redwood AE to joint-sell?
00:15:12 - Alex Kim: yes, typical is joint-sell on partner-resold deals, Redwood AE supports enterprise procurement and can join pipeline calls.
00:15:30 - Leah Chen: any notes about regional compliance for APAC?
00:15:36 - Alex Kim: APAC is supported via regions and partners; some on-prem options for data residency. we'll confirm region timelines.
00:15:48 - 00:16:20 Priya Desai: a couple of gotchas we've seen: model quantization can introduce subtle regressions - we tie quality monitoring and eval prompt sets to regression alerts in Optimize so partners can detect issues after a rollout.
00:16:30 - Marco Ruiz: good, can we get a sample of that eval process?
00:16:35 - Priya Desai: yes, we'll share a sample eval harness and suggested prompt sets.
00:16:50 - 00:17:20 Speaker 4 (Marco): on billing integration, do you have APIs for usage reporting so Vento could invoice customers with a combined invoice?
00:17:21 - Alex Kim: we can share usage APIs and partner billing exports; many partners take a combined invoice approach or use reseller billing.
00:17:40 - Samir Patel: security: do you support SAML/SSO, SCIM, and SCIM provisioning?
00:17:46 - Alex Kim: yes SAML/SSO and SCIM are supported; enterprise tier has SCIM provisioning hooks and groups.
00:17:55 - 00:18:30 Leah Chen: ok sounds like we have a good initial fit. logistics for pilot: what's typical timeline?
00:18:33 - Priya Desai: pilot 4-6 weeks typical: week 1 network + access, week 2 onboarding models + baseline tests, week 3 optimization and quantization tests, week 4 shared report and success metrics.
00:18:50 - Marco Ruiz: good. we'll plan for a mid-Feb pilot.
00:19:00 - 00:19:40 Alex Kim: next steps recap: I'll send partnership deck and pricing; Priya will send benchmark plan and required artifacts; Leah will share test cluster details; schedule technical deep dive for wk of Jan 19.
00:19:50 - Marco Ruiz: agreed. couple of smaller asks: want to see recent Redwood case study and SOC2 docs.
00:19:58 - Alex Kim: we'll include links to case study and security pack in the follow-up email.
00:20:10 - 00:20:40 Priya Desai: do you want an initial lightweight benchmark run on a Vento node or do you prefer we run in Redwood-hosted env first?
00:20:45 - Leah Chen: let's do on Vento node to validate infra interactions.
00:20:50 - Priya Desai: fine, we'll need SSH or container access details.
00:21:05 - 00:21:50 Samir Patel: can you share a sample NDA or MSA to speed legal?
00:21:53 - Alex Kim: yes we'll share a partner MSA template and NDA. legal will follow up.
00:22:10 - 00:22:55 Marco Ruiz: ok that covers most of it, any final technical notes?
00:22:58 - Priya Desai: nothing else here - we'll capture requirements and come back with a bench plan.
00:23:08 - Alex Kim: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with an email and docs.
00:23:20 - 00:23:40 Marco Ruiz: thanks Alex and Priya, excited to get started.
00:23:50 - END OF TRANSCRIPT (brief auto-summary may be present)
